passage: I'm Kabir, and I live in the flat above Zubin's. On Sunday I heard shouting through the open window and went out on the balcony. His sister Afreen was standing by the door, eyes wet. "Everyone loves you. You get everything. I wish you weren't my brother." I flinched. Zubin didn't shout back. He put his cup down. "Afreen, I know it feels unfair. I don't think it is right either." She slammed the door of her room. He sat there a while. Later I saw him knock on his father's study. I don't know what he said, and I can't say what he felt. But he didn't say one word to hit her back.

qa.q: Where did Kabir live in relation to Zubin's flat?
qa.a: Kabir lives in the flat above Zubin's.

qa.q: What might Afreen have been feeling when she said she wished Zubin wasn't her brother?
qa.a: Probably hurt and left out, since her eyes were wet and she said everyone loves him and he gets everything. Kabir can't be sure what is under her words.

qa.q: What did Zubin do that helped instead of making things worse?
qa.a: He did not retaliate. He acknowledged that it feels unfair and went to talk to his father, so the parent could address it.

qa.q: How might Zubin have seen Afreen's outburst?
qa.a: He seems to have treated it as real hurt rather than an attack, saying he knew it felt unfair and did not think it was right either, instead of shouting back.

grounding: Shows a teen whose sibling says cruel things over parental preference, seen by a neighbour, who doesn't retaliate and turns to a parent.

passage:
Daniel's brother Yosef was waiting in the hallway of their Toronto apartment when Daniel came back from the award evening.
"Congratulations, Mum's perfect son," Yosef said. "Must be nice being the one they actually like." Then, quieter and worse: "I wish you'd never been born."
Daniel's face burned. He had a sharp answer ready: at least I'm not failing three subjects. He swallowed it.
He noticed Yosef's eyes were red. He remembered Dad at dinner saying, "Why can't you be more like Daniel?" twice that week.
"I didn't ask them to say that stuff," Daniel said. "It's not fair to you. I know."
Yosef slammed his door anyway.
Later Daniel found Mum and Dad in the kitchen. "You have to stop comparing us," he said. "Yosef hates me because of it, and honestly, I'd hate me too." Mum set down her tea. Dad started to argue, then stopped.

qa.q: What did Daniel's parents do at dinner that week?
qa.a: Dad said, "Why can't you be more like Daniel?" twice.

qa.q: What was Daniel feeling when Yosef said the cruel words?
qa.a: He felt hurt and angry, with a sharp reply ready, but he held it back once he noticed the pain in Yosef's red eyes.

qa.q: What wise steps did Daniel take after the fight?
qa.a: He chose not to retaliate, told Yosef he understood it was unfair, and asked his parents directly to stop comparing them.

qa.q: How does Yosef see Daniel after the award evening?
qa.a: Yosef sees Daniel as the preferred son who takes all the love, and his cruelty comes from feeling unwanted and compared.

grounding: A preferred teen whose brother says cruel things sees the pain underneath, doesn't retaliate, and asks his parents to change.

passage:
Pema, the hostel warden, found Yash sitting on the laundry-room steps after lights-out.
His younger brother Kunal, two classes below, had shouted at him in front of the whole dining hall. "Papa's precious topper! Go back to your special phone calls. Nobody asked you to be born first." Some boys had laughed.
"I could have said worse," Yash told Pema. "About his marks. About him crying on the first night here." He hadn't. He'd walked out.
"Why do you think he said it?"
Yash picked at a thread. "Papa calls me every Sunday. He calls Kunal when he remembers."
Pema nodded. "That's pain, not just meanness. Walking away was strong. Do you want to tell your father what it's doing to Kunal?"
Pema sat with him in the office while he phoned home. "Papa, you need to call Kunal the same as me," Yash said. "He's hurting. It's not his fault."

qa.q: Where did Pema find Yash after lights-out?
How did Yash feel after Kunal shouted at him in the dining hall?
qa.a: He felt hurt and humiliated, and tempted to hit back, but he chose to walk away instead.

qa.q: How did Pema support Yash wisely?
qa.a: By helping him see Kunal's pain, praising him for not retaliating, and staying with him while he asked his father to change.

qa.q: Why might Kunal have shouted at Yash?
qa.a: Kunal seems hurt and jealous because Papa calls Yash every Sunday but calls Kunal only when he remembers.

grounding: A preferred teen whose brother says cruel things sees the pain beneath them, avoids retaliating, and asks their father to change.
